n1.text: Is there an ordered search space — a sorted array, or a range of candidate answers?

n2.text: Is there a yes/no test that, once it flips, never flips back (a monotonic predicate)?

n3.text: Are you searching an array for a value, or searching a range of possible answers?

options.label: A range of answers ('minimum X such that…')

n4.text: Do you need an exact match, or the first/last position satisfying a condition?

r-exact.detail: while (low <= high) with low = mid+1 / high = mid-1. Use the overflow-safe midpoint.

r-boundary.detail: while (low < high) with high = mid (keep mid — it may be the boundary) and low = mid+1. `low` is the answer on exit.

r-answer.detail: Binary search the candidate range; each probe runs a feasibility check. Total O(n log range). Watch for overflow in the feasibility function.

r-no.detail: Without monotonicity, halving can discard the answer. Consider hashing, a linear scan, or sorting first if you will search many times.
